links.outcome: Hallucination and false findings in AI-generated chest X-ray reports rated by radiologists
links.effect: M4CXR showed fewer hallucinations than ChatGPT; diagnostic acceptability was about 60-62% for M4CXR versus 42-45% for ChatGPT, so many reports were unacceptable.
links.quote: For diagnostic accuracy, M4CXR achieved approximately 60-62% acceptability ratings compared to ChatGPT's 42-45%.

links.outcome: Comparison of specialized CXR model versus general-purpose ChatGPT-4o on the same images
links.effect: M4CXR outperformed ChatGPT across all metrics; anatomical localization accuracy 76-77.5% vs 36-36.5%; diagnostic acceptability 60-62% vs 42-45%.
links.quote: M4CXR showed better performance in anatomical localization (76-77.5% accuracy) compared to ChatGPT (36-36.5%) and demonstrated fewer instances of hallucination.

screen.reason: The study compares the performance and hallucination rates of two AI models (M4CXR and GPT-4o) on retrospective chest X-rays evaluated by radiologists, without evaluating a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
